why: Neither brief breaks either must_not item. Checks 1–3 all run the program (`node $BIN a.jsonl bad.jsonl b.jsonl`, `printf ... | node $BIN -`, `node $BIN a.jsonl missing.jsonl b.jsonl`), so no behaviour line passes on a code read alone. The PASS/FAIL conditions stay within their lines. Check 3 only asks for "a message on stderr", not exact wording. Check 4 only asks that the lint function is unchanged. Check 6 asks for one PR, the Closes line and green tests, with no branch-name or file-limit rule. The mutation test and the exit-precedence check are under "Advisory (not pass/fail)". The builder brief does suggest a stderr wording, but it is guidance for the builder, not a PASS/FAIL condition. Check 1's argument-order and same-format requirements come straight from line 1 ("in order", "as for one file before").
